title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider (v2)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark numbers vs baseline provider (VendorX). Covered P50/P95 latency, steady-state throughput, impact of batching and quantization, KV prefix caching, and security questions (SOC2/KMS/VPC). Agreed to run a staging test on Dedicated pool next week and share SOC2 + benchmark spreadsheet. Action items assigned.
action_items: Samir Patel - Share raw benchmark logs + runner config - 2026-08-27
Avery Chen - Send updated pricing + staging Dedicated options - 2026-08-28
Maria Lopez - Confirm list of production prompts for next run - 2026-08-26
Tom Bryant - Provide network & VPC constraints doc - 2026-08-31
next_steps: Schedule staging benchmark on Dedicated pool (Avery to propose slots)
Redwood to share SOC2 + KMS integration docs
Customer to send canonical prompt set and latency SLOs
header: Date: 2026-08-25 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (Astra Head of ML), Tom Bryant (Astra Platform Eng), Nadia Singh (Astra CTO)
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, sorry slight delay on our side. Welcome back to the weekly POC sync.
[00:12] Maria Lopez: No problem, we were wrapping up a sprint so all good.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Quick agenda, run through the numbers we dropped in the spreadsheet, highlight where Redwood diverges vs VendorX baseline, then tuning suggestions, then security questions.
[00:28] Tom Bryant: Sounds good. we pulled the latest runner logs this morning.
[00:33] Avery Chen: Great, Samir do you want to share the p50/p95 numbers? I put the sheet link in chat but it's also in the deck we referenced.
[00:42] Samir Patel: Yeah, so high level: using the canonical prompt set Maria sent last week (thanks), baseline provider VendorX median was about 120ms p50 and p95 around 480ms at the 200 TPS synthetic load. Redwood in hosted mode with default config measured p50 ~140ms and p95 ~320ms. Our optimized config (int8 quant + batching tweaks + prefix cache) got p50 down to 110ms and p95 to ~270ms.
[01:10] Maria Lopez: Okay interesting, VendorX p50 lower but p95 worse. Is that steady-state or burst numbers?
[01:18] Samir Patel: Good question. Baseline numbers we have are steady-state measured across 10 minutes at 200 TPS. VendorX shows more variance at the tail. Redwood's continuous batching and KV/prefix cache helps reduce tail. In Dedicated mode we expect further tail improvements.
[01:35] Tom Bryant: Can you explain what you changed for the "optimized" config?
[01:40] Samir Patel: Sure. Three levers: 1) int8 quant profile for the model to reduce single-token compute time; 2) dynamic batching policy tuned to your request length distribution (we saw a lot of medium-length requests so we bumped max batch to 16 and latency cap 250ms); 3) KV prefix caching - for repeated prefixes we keep warmed KV across requests so we avoid cold kv restores. Also we pinned kernel selection to a lower-latency path for short sequences.
[02:05] Maria Lopez: Were there any regression in quality from int8? We care about hallucination and answer fidelity.
[02:11] Samir Patel: We ran the small eval set: ROUGE/semantic similarity delta within margin, we saw one edge case where the model sometimes trimmed a phrase - we flagged those prompts. We can run your production checks.
[02:22] Nadia Singh: Quick security question: how does KMS integration look for the Dedicated option? We need customer-managed keys for EU data.
[02:28] Avery Chen: Good callout. For Dedicated and Private we support customer KMS/HSM integration; we have doc links in the repo. I'll share the SOC2 plus our KMS guide after the call.
[02:40] Tom Bryant: Also need audit logs retention - our compliance team asked for 1 year of request/response logs. Does Redwood support that out of the box?
[02:48] Samir Patel: Audit logs are available, retention is configurable as an add-on. For Private deployments you can export logs to your S3 and keep them indefinitely. For hosted we currently offer up to 180 days default, with enterprise add-on to extend to 1 year.
[03:05] Maria Lopez: Cool. Back to the numbers - throughput, steady state.
[03:12] Samir Patel: Throughput wise: at 200 concurrent steady TPS, Redwood hosted default plateaued at ~190 TPS sustained. With batching and Dedicated reserved GPUs we hit stable 230 TPS with lower p95. VendorX reported dips under the same synthetic loads. One important note: their baseline used a slightly different prompt padding and batching semantics which explains some of the lower p50.
[03:40] Maria Lopez: So what should we expect if we go Dedicated for the pilot stage?
[03:44] Avery Chen: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and we can tune autoscaling/burst to match your spike patterns. For your workload we expect p95 improvements ~15-25% over hosted optimized. We'll run a staging test to validate.
[03:58] Tom Bryant: Network-wise we have a strict egress policy, we might need a VPC peering setup. Any blockers?
[04:04] Samir Patel: We support VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated; there's some initial routing setup but usually straightforward. We'll need your VPC CIDR ranges and a staging subnet to test.
[04:18] Maria Lopez: On the spreadsheet I saw a column called "cache hit rate" - what's our hit rate in the optimized run?
[04:24] Samir Patel: For your prompt distribution we saw ~42% prefix cache hit rate which translated to a roughly 18% average token cost reduction. If you can increase prefix reuse or canonicalize prompts you'll see better gains.
[04:38] Maria Lopez: Nice. Any tradeoffs on freshness with cache?
[04:42] Samir Patel: Cache TTL is configurable; for us typical is per-request session TTL. If you need strict freshness we can lower TTL but you lose some cost/latency upside.
[04:52] Avery Chen: Quick interruption, there are a couple of odd transcriptions in the spreadsheet I want to flag ("k v cache" spelled as kvac) - ignore typos, we have raw logs if you want.
[05:03] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:07] Tom Bryant: On cost: can you ballpark cost delta vs VendorX on the optimized runs?
[05:12] Samir Patel: Rough numbers: per 1M tokens, VendorX came in around $X (we anonymized as baseline), Redwood hosted optimized about 8-12% lower due to batching and quantization; Dedicated with autoscaling improved cost by another ~15% for heavy sustained workloads because you avoid shared tenancy overhead. We'll send a more detailed cost spreadsheet.
[05:34] Maria Lopez: Good. For the next staging run, can we replicate VendorX's padding and batching semantics exactly so we get apples-to-apples?
[05:42] Samir Patel: Yes, we can. We logged their runner config; we can run both configs in parallel and produce side-by-side traces. That will highlight differences from network vs runtime vs kernel choices.
[05:55] Avery Chen: Let's reserve time for a canary run on Dedicated next week - Samir, what allocation do you need to emulate the 200 TPS?
[06:03] Samir Patel: For your model size and prompt distribution, recommend 8x A10-style GPUs or equivalent; for Dedicated staging a single pool with that size should work. We'll confirm exact instance families in the follow-up email.
[06:18] Maria Lopez: Are there any known compatibility issues with our model infra? We have on-prem model weights in a private registry.
[06:24] Samir Patel: For Private deployments we support loading from your registry and air-gapped setups. For hosted/Dedicated we can ingest model artifacts via secure upload or customer S3 with presigned URLs, and we can integrate with your registry via VPC. We'll need a short checklist which I'll share.
[06:40] Tom Bryant: About SSO and RBAC, our security team requires SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[06:45] Avery Chen: Redwood supports SAML-based SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in enterprise plans. RBAC roles are configurable at route-level. We'll include our SSO onboarding doc.
[06:56] Maria Lopez: A quick question on fallback policies: if Dedicated capacity is temporarily unreachable do requests failover to hosted?
[07:03] Samir Patel: Yes you can configure smart routing with automatic fallback to compatible hosted variants; there's policy controls for cost tiering and region fallback. Failover behavior is atomic per-route.
[07:15] Speaker 2: (overlap)
[07:18] Maria Lopez: Ok great. Any surprises in the logs - memory spikes or OOMs?
[07:23] Samir Patel: No OOMs in these runs. We saw a couple of kernel-choice warnings under the VendorX config when sequence len spiked which led to tail latency. We adjusted kernel pinning to avoid that.
[07:35] Tom Bryant: For the dedicated run, what's the expected lead time to provision?
[07:39] Avery Chen: Typically 3-5 business days for staging pools, faster if we re-use existing pools. We'll confirm availability in the follow-up.
[07:50] Maria Lopez: I wanted to bring up the eval suite - we run a hallucination regression test nightly. Can Redwood ingest those eval runs and alert if quantization causes regression?
[07:59] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties eval sets to deployments; you can set regression thresholds and get alerts. For the POC we can hook your nightly eval to the POC pipeline.
[08:12] Nadia Singh: Another compliance note: we need data residency in the EU for production. Does Dedicated in EU region support that?
[08:19] Avery Chen: Yes. We have EU region Dedicated and Private deployments, and we can pin routing to EU-only. We'll need to confirm the region for staging.
[08:30] Maria Lopez: Back to the p95 numbers - can you share the actual latency distribution chart? I saw a boxplot but want raw percentiles.
[08:38] Samir Patel: I put percentiles in the spreadsheet: p50, p75, p90, p95, p99. I'll upload the raw histogram and the runner's CSVs.
[08:48] Tom Bryant: From an ops perspective, what error budgets do you recommend we set during pilot?
[08:53] Samir Patel: For pilot I'd recommend p95 < 350ms and error rate < 0.5% initially. We'll tune after the first week of staging.
[09:02] Maria Lopez: That sounds reasonable. If we can't hit that, what are fallback options?
[09:06] Avery Chen: We can route traffic to a higher-capacity model variant for degraded quality but lower latency, or to VendorX temporarily if needed - though that adds switching complexity. Ideally Dedicated eliminates that need.
[09:20] Tom Bryant: Any notes about request shaping? We have some heavy analytic prompts we can isolate.
[09:25] Samir Patel: Yes, isolating long-horizon analytic prompts into a separate route prevents them from affecting batch latency for short interactive prompts. We can create separate routes with different SLOs.
[09:38] Maria Lopez: Ok let's talk scheduling - next staging window?
[09:42] Avery Chen: Propose next Tuesday 14:00 UTC for a 2-hour staging run. I'll send a calendar hold after we agree.
[09:50] Maria Lopez: Works for me.
[09:52] Tom Bryant: Works here too.
[09:54] Nadia Singh: I'll ask compliance to join for the first 30 minutes.
[09:58] Avery Chen: Perfect. Quick housekeeping, I'm going to list the deliverables: Samir share logs + runner config; Avery share SOC2/KMS + pricing; Maria confirm prompt set; Tom share VPC constraints. Anything else?
[10:12] Maria Lopez: Could you also include a sample canary routing policy? We want to see an A/B config.
[10:18] Samir Patel: Yep I'll include a sample canary config and the rollout steps.
[10:22] Speaker 3: (mumbled)
[10:26] Avery Chen: Any final concerns or blockers?
[10:30] Tom Bryant: None from infra, just need the VPC details after the call.
[10:34] Maria Lopez: No blockers. We'll aim to get the canonical prompts to you by Thursday.
[10:39] Avery Chen: Great. Let's recap next steps and action items - I'll read them out.
[10:44] Avery Chen: Samir will share the raw benchmark logs and runner config by Friday (2026-08-27). Avery will send SOC2 and KMS docs and updated pricing by Saturday (2026-08-28). Maria will confirm production prompt set by Thursday (2026-08-26). Tom will provide VPC constraints doc by end of the month (2026-08-31). We'll run a Dedicated staging window next Tuesday 14:00 UTC.
[11:10] Maria Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[11:13] Nadia Singh: Thanks.
[11:15] Avery Chen: Thanks all, will follow up in email with the sheet and calendar invite.
[11:20] (call ends)
